Theme

Money, work & business · Household, washing & chores

tenant noun

also tenants, lodger, renter

classical

Cic. Phil. 2.105: tē inquilīnō (nōn enim dominō)
Suet. Ner. 44.2: inquilīnōs prīvātārum aedium atque īnsulārum, tenants of private houses and of blocks of flats

inquilīnus, inquilīnī m.

noun, second declension

tenant, lodger

One who lives in a place not his own (Lewis & Short), set against the owner, dominus.

Other words

  • conductor, conductōris m. — the one who rents; a tenant of a house or farm

    noun, third declension · also used · classical · Caes. BC 3.21.1: mercēdēs habitātiōnum annuās conductōribus dōnāvit; Cic. Att. 12.32.2: conductōrēs quī sint et quantī, who the tenants are and what they pay

    The party who condūcit, rents (see rent, pay to use); also one who hires workers (see employer).

  • colōnus, colōnī m. — a tenant farmer

    noun, second declension · also used · classical · Cic. Caecin. 94: quī colōnus habuit conductum dē Caesenniā fundum, who as tenant farmer had rented the farm from Caesennia

    Properly a farmer; one who farms land that he rents.

Examples

  • essedās trānscurrentēs pōnō et fabrum inquilīnum et serrārium vīcīnum

    I count in the carriages rattling past, the carpenter who lodges in the building and the sawyer next doorSen. Ep. 56.4

  • Partem etiam cēnsūs omnēs ōrdinēs cōnferre jussit et īnsuper inquilīnōs prīvātārum aedium atque īnsulārum pēnsiōnem annuam repraesentāre fiscō

    He also ordered every class to contribute part of its property, and tenants of private houses and of blocks of flats to pay a year’s rent to the treasury at onceSuet. Ner. 44.2

  • At vērō tē inquilīnō (nōn enim dominō) personābant omnia vōcibus ēbriōrum

    But with you as tenant (for you were not the owner) the whole house rang with drunken voicesCic. Phil. 2.105

See also landlord, rent, rent, house.
